name: Alex Cusumano
title: Associate Professor of Chemistry & Director of Graduate Studies
bio: Prof. Cusumano serves as Director of Graduate Studies for the Department of Chemistry. His laboratory develops novel synthetic methodology for functional peptides, macrocyclic scaffolds, and chemical probes targeting aberrant signaling pathways in oncogenesis.
publications: Modular Assembly of Cyclic Peptide Libraries for Target Deconvolution, J. Am. Chem. Soc. (2024)
Kinetic Profiling of Interfacial Bioconjugation in Cellular Milieu, Chem. Sci. (2022)

name: Chuan He
title: John T. Wilson Distinguished Service Professor
bio: Prof. He is world-renowned for discovering reversible RNA methylation, pioneering the field of epitranscriptomics. The He Laboratory elucidates the biochemical roles of RNA modifications in gene expression regulation, human disease, and agricultural yield enhancement.
publications: Reversible RNA methylation in mammalian gene expression regulation, Nature (2023)
Fate and function of modified m6A transcripts in embryonic development, Cell (2021)

name: Laura Gagliardi
title: Richard and Kathy Leventhal Professor of Chemistry & Molecular Engineering
bio: Prof. Gagliardi develops electronic structure theories and multi-reference quantum chemical methods to model complex chemical systems, photocatalysis, actinide chemistry, and gas separations in porous materials.
publications: Multiconfiguration Pair-Density Functional Theory for Actinides, J. Chem. Theory Comput. (2024)
Predicting gas adsorption isotherms in metal-organic frameworks via quantum mechanics, Science (2022)

name: Jack W. Szostak
title: University Professor of Chemistry
accolades: Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine (2009)
bio: Nobel Laureate Jack Szostak investigates the chemical origins of life. His laboratory designs autonomous protocell systems capable of Darwinian evolution, non-enzymatic RNA replication, and self-assembling fatty acid vesicles.
publications: Non-enzymatic replication of genetic polymers in primitive cell membranes, Nature Chemistry (2023)
Prebiotic synthesis of activated nucleotides under hydrothermal simulation, PNAS (2022)

name: Bryan C. Dickinson
title: Professor of Chemistry
bio: The Dickinson group develops molecular technologies to probe and control biological systems. Research focuses on genetically encoded biosensors, split-luciferases, proximity labeling enzymes, and targeted RNA therapeutics.
publications: Proximity-dependent RNA-protein labeling in live mammalian cells, Nat. Methods (2024)
Programmable deaminase switches for engineered cellular control, Nat. Chem. Biol. (2022)

name: Bozhi Tian
title: Professor of Chemistry
bio: Prof. Tian explores physical biology and nano-biointerfaces. His lab synthesizes biomimetic silicon materials and soft hydrogels for optical neuromodulation, cardiac pacing, and cellular biomechanics.
publications: Monolithic silicon meshes for non-genetic optoelectronic modulation of brain circuits, Nature (2023)
Soft biomimetic conductors for continuous electrophysiological recording, Science Advances (2021)

name: Gregory A. Voth
title: Haig P. Papazian Distinguished Service Professor
office: Gordon Center for Integrative Science E205
bio: Prof. Voth is a pioneer in multiscale theoretical and computational simulation methods. His group models complex biomolecular assemblies including viral capsids, actin filaments, and charge translocation pathways.
publications: Atomistic and coarse-grained dynamics of intact HIV-1 capsid maturation, Nature Struct. Mol. Biol. (2024)
Ultra-coarse-grained modeling of protein condensates, Biophysical J. (2022)

name: Andrei Tokmakoff
title: Henry G. Gale Distinguished Service Professor
bio: The Tokmakoff Laboratory uses ultrafast multi-dimensional infrared spectroscopy to study the hydrogen-bonding dynamics of liquid water, protein folding and conformational transitions, and aqueous proton hydration.
publications: Two-dimensional infrared spectroscopy of the hydrated excess proton in water, Science (2023)
Mapping transient secondary structure in protein folding intermediates, JACS (2022)

name: Yamuna Krishnan
title: Professor of Chemistry
bio: Prof. Krishnan creates DNA-based nanodevices that operate inside living cells and model organisms to map chemical environments—such as pH, chloride, and second messengers—within designated subcellular organelles.
publications: Quantitative mapping of ionic dynamics in endosomes via DNA nanodevices, Nature Nanotech. (2023)
Targeted subcellular imaging of lipid flux in disease models, Cell Chem. Biol. (2021)

name: Jiwoong Park
title: Professor and Chair of Chemistry & Molecular Engineering
bio: Prof. Park directs research on the science and technology of atomically thin 2D materials. His laboratory synthesizes continuous wafer-scale 2D transition metal dichalcogenides and examines their quantum transport properties.
publications: High-mobility wafer-scale 2D semiconductors for next-generation logic, Nature Materials (2023)
Thermal conductivity anomalies in single-layer van der Waals heterostructures, Science (2021)

name: Paul Alivisatos
title: President, University of Chicago; John D. MacArthur Distinguished Service Professor
bio: Paul Alivisatos is the 14th President of the University of Chicago and an internationally renowned pioneer in the synthesis and fabrication of semiconductor and metallic nanocrystals with applications in renewable energy and quantum photonics.
publications: Scalable synthesis and facet control of colloidal semiconductor nanocrystals, Chem. Rev. (2022)
Dynamic transformations of colloidal nanocrystals under in situ liquid-cell electron microscopy, Science (2020)

name: Mark Levin
title: Associate Professor of Chemistry
bio: Prof. Levin pioneered modern methods of single-atom skeletal editing, permitting direct insertion, deletion, and transmutation of atoms within complex heterocyclic molecules without breaking the peripheral architecture.
publications: Single-atom skeletal editing of aromatic rings via nitrogen insertion, Science (2023)
Carbon-to-nitrogen transmutation in drug-like scaffolds, Nature (2021)

name: Anna Wuttig
title: Assistant Professor of Chemistry
accolades: Packard Fellow in Science and Engineering
bio: The Wuttig group studies interfacial chemical dynamics to drive sustainable electrocatalysis, focusing on electricity-driven chemical conversions for carbon neutrality, clean fuel production, and value-added organic synthesis.
publications: Proton-coupled electron transfer in electrocatalytic CO2 reduction, JACS (2023)
Interfacial electric fields govern selectivity in electrosynthetic coupling, Nature Catalysis (2022)

name: Aaron Dinner
title: Professor of Chemistry
bio: Prof. Dinner develops multiscale physical and data-driven methods to understand cellular organization, molecular motor dynamics, nonequilibrium statistical mechanics, and chromatin architecture.
publications: Deep learning frameworks for rare event sampling in biopolymer folding, Nat. Comput. Sci. (2023)
Actomyosin network contractions under boundary confinement, Biophys. J. (2021)

name: Dmitri V. Talapin
title: Ernest DeWitt Burton Distinguished Service Professor
bio: Prof. Talapin's research focuses on the chemistry and physics of colloidal nanostructures. His lab designs self-assembled electronic superlattices, 2D MXenes, and covalent surface engineering methods for quantum electronics.
publications: Covalently bonded colloidal quantum dot solids for electronic transport, Science (2023)
Direct optical lithography of functional inorganic nanomaterials, Science (2020)

name: Michael J. Franklin
title: Liew Family Chairman and Professor of Computer Science; Senior Advisor to the Provost
accolades: SIGMOD Edgar F. Codd Innovations Award
bio: Prof. Franklin is an authority on distributed data systems and co-creator of Apache Spark and AMPLab. At UChicago, he heads the expansion of the CS department and data science initiatives across campus.
publications: Next-Generation Data Architecture for Collaborative Scientific Discovery, ACM SIGMOD (2024)
High-Throughput Analytics over Federated Cloud Datastores, VLDB (2022)

name: Fred Chong
title: Seymour Goodman Professor of Computer Science
accolades: Lead PI of EPiQC NSF Expedition
bio: Prof. Chong leads the Enabling Practical-scale Quantum Computing (EPiQC) project. His research bridges the gap between quantum algorithms and real-world noisy intermediate-scale quantum (NISQ) hardware.
publications: Co-designing Quantum Algorithms and Pulse-Level Compilers, IEEE Micro (2023)
Noise-Aware Compilation for Multi-Qubit Systems, ACM ASPLOS (2022)

name: Rebecca Willett
title: Professor of Computer Science and Statistics; Director of AI at DSI
bio: Prof. Willett develops machine learning algorithms for ill-posed inverse problems and high-dimensional data, with applications ranging from medical imaging reconstruction to climate modeling.
publications: Provable guarantees for deep neural network inverse imaging, SIAM J. Math. Data Sci. (2023)
Physics-informed self-supervised learning for scientific discovery, NeurIPS (2022)

name: Shan Lu
degrees: Ph.D., University of Illinois at Urbana-Champaign
title: Professor of Computer Science
bio: Prof. Lu designs automated program analysis, testing, and debugging systems to eliminate concurrency bugs, performance degradations, and non-deterministic faults in distributed web infrastructure.
publications: Automated detection of performance anti-patterns in cloud microservices, ACM SOSP (2023)
Diagnosing concurrency bugs through state-machine tracing, ACM OSDI (2021)

name: Pedro Lopes
title: Associate Professor of Computer Science
bio: Prof. Lopes leads the Human Computer Integration Lab. He pioneers wearable interactive devices that physically integrate with the human body via electrical muscle stimulation and sensory actuation.
publications: Integrating wearable haptics directly into the musculoskeletal system, ACM CHI (2024)
Chemical haptics: Rendered olfactory and thermal sensations via topical triggers, ACM UIST (2022)

name: Young-Kee Kim
title: Louis Block Distinguished Service Professor of Physics; President of the APS
bio: Prof. Kim is an experimental particle physicist studying the fundamental building blocks of matter and the forces governing the universe, leading major experiments at Fermilab's Tevatron and CERN's Large Hadron Collider.
publications: High-precision measurement of the W-boson mass with the CDF II detector, Science (2022)
Searches for new physics with the ATLAS detector at 13 TeV, Phys. Rev. Lett. (2021)

name: Dam Thanh Son
degrees: Ph.D., Institute for Nuclear Research, Moscow
title: University Professor of Physics
bio: Prof. Son is renowned for applying string theory and gauge/gravity duality to strongly coupled quantum systems, including quark-gluon plasmas, fractional quantum Hall states, and unitary Fermi gases.
publications: Composite fermion theory and particle-hole symmetry in quantum Hall effect, Phys. Rev. X (2023)
Universal bounds on viscosity-to-entropy ratio from black hole thermodynamics, Phys. Rev. Lett. (2021)

name: Ngô Bảo Châu
title: Francis and Rose Yuen Distinguished Service Professor
bio: Fields Medalist Ngô Bảo Châu is celebrated for his proof of the Fundamental Lemma in the Langlands Program, introducing novel algebro-geometric methods through Hitchin fibrations.
publications: The Fundamental Lemma for Lie Algebras, Publications Mathématiques de l'IHÉS (2022)
Hitchin fibrations and orbital integrals, Duke Math. J. (2020)

name: Carlos Kenig
title: Louis Block Distinguished Service Professor of Mathematics; Former President of the IMU
accolades: Former President of International Mathematical Union
bio: Prof. Kenig is an international leader in harmonic analysis and partial differential equations, having served as President of the International Mathematical Union (IMU) from 2019 to 2022.
publications: Energy critical wave equations in non-convex domains, Ann. of Math. (2023)
Global well-posedness and scattering for nonlinear Schrödinger equations, Invent. Math. (2021)

name: Wendy Freedman
title: University Professor of Astronomy and Astrophysics
bio: Prof. Freedman is an observational cosmologist famous for leading the Hubble Space Telescope Key Project to measure the expansion rate of the universe (the Hubble constant) and current JWST distance calibrator surveys.
publications: Measurements of the Hubble Constant with the James Webb Space Telescope, Astrophys. J. (2024)
The Carnegie-Chicago Hubble Program: Final Results, Astrophys. J. (2021)

name: Rina Foygel Barber
title: Louis Block Professor of Statistics
bio: MacArthur 'Genius' Fellow Rina Foygel Barber develops innovative statistical methods for uncertainty quantification, distribution-free prediction bands, and variable selection in high-dimensional datasets.
publications: Conformal prediction with distribution shift, Ann. Statist. (2023)
Controlling the false discovery rate via knockoffs in high dimensions, J. R. Stat. Soc. B (2021)

name: Yoav Gilad
title: Professor of Human Genetics & Medicine; Dean of Biomedical Research
bio: Prof. Gilad investigates the genetic mechanisms that drive differences in gene expression between human populations and primates, combining induced pluripotent stem cells (iPSCs) with high-throughput sequencing.
publications: Dynamic eQTLs in human cardiomyocyte differentiation, Science (2023)
Dissecting single-cell regulatory variation across primate tissues, Nature Genetics (2021)

name: Olufunmilayo Olopade
title: Walter L. Palmer Distinguished Service Professor of Medicine & Human Genetics
bio: Dr. Olopade is a MacArthur Fellow and global pioneer in cancer genetics. Her research has transformed the understanding of BRCA1 and BRCA2 mutations in breast cancer risk among women of African descent.
publications: Genomic characterization of triple-negative breast cancer in diverse populations, Nat. Rev. Clin. Oncol. (2023)
Polygenic risk scores for breast cancer risk prediction in women of African ancestry, J. Clin. Oncol. (2022)

name: Peggy Mason
title: Professor of Neurobiology
bio: Prof. Mason studies the neural circuits underlying pro-social helping behavior, empathy, and pain modulation in mammals, showing that rodents will liberate distressed cage-mates driven by shared affect.
publications: Neural circuits of empathy-driven helping behavior in rodents, Science (2021)
Descending serotonergic modulation of spinal nociceptive processing, J. Neurosci. (2020)

name: Tobin Sosnick
title: William B. Graham Professor and Chair of Biochemistry & Molecular Biology
department: Department of Biochemistry and Molecular Biology
bio: Prof. Sosnick combines biophysical experiments and computational simulations to delineate the folding trajectories of proteins and RNAs, and engineers optogenetic switches for light-activated cellular control.
publications: Resolving the transition state ensemble in de novo protein design, PNAS (2023)
Engineered light-controlled dimerization switches in mammalian cells, Nat. Chem. Biol. (2021)

name: James J. Heckman
title: Henry Schultz Distinguished Service Professor of Economics
department: Kenneth C. Griffin Department of Economics
bio: Nobel Laureate James Heckman developed the celebrated 'Heckman two-step correction' for selection bias and has spent decades proving the transformative economic and social returns of early childhood investment.
publications: The Lifecycle Returns to Early Childhood Programs, J. Polit. Econ. (2023)
Microeconometric Methods for Policy Evaluation, Econometrica (2021)

name: Michael Kremer
title: University Professor in Economics and the Harris School; Director of Development Innovation Lab
department: Kenneth C. Griffin Department of Economics & Harris
bio: Nobel Laureate Michael Kremer pioneered experimental approaches to alleviating global poverty. His work shaped the Advance Market Commitment for pneumococcal vaccines, saving over 700,000 lives worldwide.
publications: Market Shaping for Pandemic Preparedness and Global Public Goods, Science (2023)
Experimental Evidence on Water Quality Interventions and Child Mortality, Q. J. Econ. (2022)

name: John A. List
title: Kenneth C. Griffin Distinguished Service Professor of Economics
department: Kenneth C. Griffin Department of Economics
bio: Prof. List is the world's foremost pioneer in using randomized field experiments to test economic theory in everyday natural environments, from stock trading and education to corporate decision making.
publications: The Voltage Effect: How to Make Good Ideas Great and Great Ideas Scale, Currency (2022)
Field Experiments on Charitable Giving and Social Preferences, J. Polit. Econ. (2021)

name: Steven D. Levitt
title: William B. Ogden Distinguished Service Professor of Economics
department: Kenneth C. Griffin Department of Economics
bio: Prof. Levitt, winner of the John Bates Clark Medal and co-author of the best-selling book *Freakonomics*, applies empirical economic analysis to unusual real-world questions, incentives, and public policy.
publications: Head versus Heart: Quantitative Field Experiments on Critical Decision Making, Rev. Econ. Stud. (2021)
Testing Behavioral Economic Models in Competitive Sports Markets, J. Polit. Econ. (2019)

name: John J. Mearsheimer
title: R. Wendell Harrison Distinguished Service Professor of Political Science
bio: Prof. Mearsheimer is the leading theorist of offensive realism. His seminal treatises include *The Tragedy of Great Power Politics*, *The Great Delusion*, and *The Israel Lobby and U.S. Foreign Policy*.
publications: The Inevitable Rivalry: America, China, and the Tragedy of Great Power Politics, Foreign Affairs (2021)
Bound to Fail: The Rise and Fall of the Liberal International Order, Int. Security (2019)

name: Mario L. Small
title: Professor of Sociology
accolades: American Academy of Political and Social Science
bio: Prof. Small investigates urban poverty, social networks, and organizational ties. He has authored award-winning books including *Villa Victoria*, *Unanticipated Gains*, and *Someone To Talk To*.
publications: Personal networks and cognitive empathy under economic strain, Am. J. Sociol. (2023)
The Structure of Social Capital in Disadvantaged Urban Communities, Annu. Rev. Sociol. (2021)

name: Martha C. Nussbaum
title: Ernst Freund Distinguished Service Professor of Law and Ethics
bio: Prof. Nussbaum is one of the world's most preeminent living philosophers. Co-creator of the Human Development Capabilities Approach, her groundbreaking works bridge ancient philosophy, political justice, and global rights.
publications: Justice for Animals: Our Collective Responsibility, Simon & Schuster (2023)
The Monarchy of Fear: A Philosopher Looks at Our Political Crisis, Simon & Schuster (2018)

name: Robert B. Pippin
title: Evelyn Stefansson Nef Distinguished Service Professor of Social Thought & Philosophy
bio: Prof. Pippin is renowned for his influential re-interpretation of German Idealism, modern subjectivity, and philosophical studies of visual modernism, literature, and American cinema.
publications: The Culmination: Heidegger, German Idealism, and the Fate of Philosophy, UChicago Press (2024)
Hegel's Realm of Shadows: Logic as Metaphysics in the Science of Logic, UChicago Press (2019)

name: W.J.T. Mitchell
title: Gaylord Donnelley Distinguished Service Professor of English and Art History
bio: Prof. Mitchell has served as editor of the influential journal *Critical Inquiry* since 1978. His works on the 'pictorial turn' and iconology are cornerstones in contemporary art history and visual media studies.
publications: What Do Pictures Want? The Lives and Loves of Images, UChicago Press
Image Science: Iconology, Visual Culture, and Media Aesthetics, UChicago Press

name: Wu Hung
title: Harrie A. Vanderstappen Distinguished Service Professor of Art History
accolades: Director of Center for the Art of East Asia
bio: Prof. Wu Hung is an internationally renowned scholar of traditional and contemporary Chinese art, spearheading global exhibitions, digital preservation of Buddhist cave murals, and East Asian art historiography.
publications: Chinese Art and Dynastic Time, Princeton University Press (2022)
Space in Art History: A Global View, Oxford University Press (2020)

name: Matthew Tirrell
title: Dean Emeritus & Robert A. Millikan Distinguished Service Professor
bio: Founding Dean of PME, Prof. Tirrell pioneered the integration of physical and engineering sciences with molecular-level precision, synthesizing peptide amphiphiles for targeted atherosclerosis and oncology therapies.
publications: Peptide amphiphile micelles for targeted delivery across the blood-brain barrier, ACS Nano (2023)
Polyelectrolyte complex coacervates: Fundamentals and applications, Chem. Rev. (2021)

name: Supratik Guha
title: Professor of Molecular Engineering; Director of Center for Nanoscale Materials
bio: Prof. Guha led the development of high-k dielectric oxides at IBM that are now used in all modern silicon microprocessors. His UChicago group develops nanoscale electronic materials and ubiquitous environmental sensing networks.
publications: Autonomous sensing networks for distributed river water quality monitoring, Nat. Water (2023)
Non-volatile memory technologies via phase-change chalcogenides, Nature Reviews Materials (2021)

name: Jeffrey A. Hubbell
title: Eugene Bell Professor in Tissue Engineering
bio: Prof. Hubbell engineers biomaterials and fusion proteins that stimulate tissue regeneration or induce immune tolerance, founding multiple clinical-stage biotech enterprises for autoimmune and cancer treatment.
publications: Antigen-specific immune tolerance induced by liver-targeted polymeric nanoparticles, Nature Biomed. Eng. (2023)
Engineered cytokines with enhanced therapeutic window for cancer immunotherapy, Science Trans. Med. (2021)

name: Andrew N. Cleland
title: John A. MacLean Sr. Professor of Molecular Engineering
bio: Prof. Cleland created the world's first macroscopic mechanical resonator brought to its quantum ground state. His group develops superconducting quantum circuits and acoustic quantum memory architectures.
publications: Quantum entanglement between acoustic phonons and superconducting qubits, Nature (2023)
Controlling flying quantum acoustic states in surface acoustic wave channels, Science (2022)

name: Eugene F. Fama
title: Robert R. McCormick Distinguished Service Professor of Finance
bio: Nobel Laureate Eugene Fama is known as the 'Father of Modern Finance'. His research established the Efficient Market Hypothesis and the Fama-French multi-factor asset pricing models used across global capital markets.
publications: Contracting and Cross-Sectional Asset Pricing Anomaly Testing, J. Finance (2022)
The Efficient Capital Markets: A Half-Century Perspective, J. Polit. Econ. (2020)

name: Richard H. Thaler
title: Charles R. Walgreen Distinguished Service Professor of Behavioral Science and Economics
bio: Nobel Laureate Richard Thaler is the founding father of Behavioral Economics. His work on mental accounting, fairness, self-control, and Choice Architecture (*Nudge*) transformed global public policy and pension systems.
publications: Nudge: The Final Edition, Yale University Press (2021)
Behavioral Economics and Public Policy Choices, Q. J. Econ. (2019)

name: Douglas W. Diamond
title: Merton H. Miller Distinguished Service Professor of Finance
bio: Nobel Laureate Douglas Diamond created the foundational Diamond-Dybvig model explaining why banks exist, why they are fundamentally vulnerable to runs, and how deposit insurance mitigates systemic crises.
publications: Financial Intermediation and Financial Crises, J. Polit. Econ. (2022)
Liquidity, Liquidity Risk, and Systemic Fragility, J. Finance (2020)

name: Raghuram G. Rajan
title: Katherine Dusak Miller Distinguished Service Professor of Finance
accolades: Former Governor of Reserve Bank of India
bio: Prof. Rajan served as the 23rd Governor of the Reserve Bank of India and Chief Economist at the IMF. His research spans banking, financial sector evolution, and the economic balance between states, markets, and communities.
publications: The Third Pillar: How Markets and the State Leave the Community Behind, Penguin (2019)
Liquidity Risk and the Dynamics of Bank Intermediation, Rev. Financ. Stud. (2022)

name: Geoffrey R. Stone
title: Edward H. Levi Distinguished Service Professor of Law
accolades: Chair of Chicago Free Expression Principles
bio: Prof. Stone is an eminent constitutional scholar who chaired the committee that drafted the Chicago Principles of Free Expression—now adopted by over 100 universities. He has authored definitive treatises on civil liberties.
publications: Perilous Times: Free Speech in Wartime from the Sedition Act to the War on Terrorism, W.W. Norton
Democracy and Equality: The Enduring Constitutional Vision of the Warren Court, Oxford University Press

name: Cass R. Sunstein
title: Senior Lecturer & Karl N. Llewellyn Distinguished Service Professor Emeritus
bio: Prof. Sunstein is widely regarded as the most cited American legal scholar. He taught at UChicago for 27 years, pioneering behavioral law and economics, administrative law reform, and choice architecture.
publications: Noise: A Flaw in Human Judgment (with Daniel Kahneman & Olivier Sibony), Little, Brown (2021)
The Cost-Benefit Revolution, MIT Press (2018)

name: James A. Robinson
title: University Professor; Director of The Pearson Institute for the Study and Resolution of Global Conflicts
department: Harris School of Public Policy & Department of Political Science
bio: Nobel Laureate James Robinson is co-author of *Why Nations Fail* and *The Narrow Corridor*. His research explores the political and historical mechanisms that determine institutional divergence and long-term prosperity.
publications: The Narrow Corridor: States, Societies, and the Fate of Liberty, Penguin (2019)
Why Nations Fail: The Origins of Power, Prosperity, and Poverty, Crown Business (2012)

name: Jens Ludwig
title: Edwin A. and Betty L. Bergman Distinguished Service Professor; Director of Crime Lab
bio: Prof. Ludwig directs the UChicago Crime Lab and Education Lab, partnering with civic leaders and researchers to evaluate data-driven, evidence-based solutions that curb urban violence and expand opportunity.
publications: Machine learning can predict firearm violence and guide community violence interventions, Nature Human Behaviour (2023)
Long-term impacts of behavioral interventions for high-risk youth, Q. J. Econ. (2021)

name: Andrew L. Ferguson
title: Professor of Molecular Engineering & Vice Dean of Equity, Diversity, and Inclusion
department: Pritzker School of Molecular Engineering & Chemistry
bio: Prof. Ferguson combines molecular simulation, statistical mechanics, and machine learning to design self-assembling materials and engineer biological polymers. His group develops generative AI platforms for de novo antiviral therapeutic design.
publications: Active learning and generative models for peptide sequence optimization, Nat. Mach. Intell. (2023)
Nonlinear manifold learning for molecular kinetics and free energy landscapes, Chem. Sci. (2022)

name: Benoît Roux
title: Amgen Professor of Biochemistry and Molecular Biology & Professor of Chemistry
accolades: National Institutes of Health MERIT Award
office: Gordon Center for Integrative Science W242
bio: Prof. Roux uses theoretical and computational methods to understand the microscopic workings of biological macromolecular machines. His lab models ion selectivity and voltage-gating in potassium and sodium channels.
publications: Microscopic mechanism of voltage-dependent gating in potassium channels, Nature (2023)
Free energy calculations for biomolecular systems: In pursuit of accuracy, Chem. Rev. (2022)

name: Daniel Laorenza
title: Assistant Professor of Chemistry
bio: Prof. Laorenza develops precision synthetic synthetic routes to transition metal clusters, metal-radical networks, and solid-state materials exhibiting novel magnetic, optical, and quantum coherent phenomena.
publications: Strong magnetic coupling in mixed-valence transition metal clusters, JACS (2024)
Synthetically tunable spin-lattice relaxation in molecular quantum bits, Inorg. Chem. (2023)

name: David A. Mazziotti
title: Professor of Chemistry & The James Franck Institute
accolades: International Academy of Quantum Molecular Science
bio: Prof. Mazziotti's group develops reduced-density-matrix (RDM) mechanics to calculate the electronic structure of strongly correlated molecules without wavefunctions, implementing these algorithms on noisy intermediate-scale quantum (NISQ) computers.
publications: Quantum computational calculation of molecular excited states via reduced density matrices, Phys. Rev. Lett. (2023)
Exact contracted Schrodinger equation for strongly correlated electrons, J. Chem. Phys. (2022)

name: Dipti Jasrasaria
title: Assistant Professor of Chemistry
bio: The Jasrasaria group develops theoretical and computational tools to understand how quantum mechanical effects dictate energy and charge transport in complex, nanoscale environments like light-harvesting complexes and polaritonic cavities.
publications: Vibrational coherence and non-adiabatic transport in photosynthetic light harvesting, J. Phys. Chem. Lett. (2024)
Generalized quantum master equations for condensed-phase excitonic systems, Chem. Sci. (2023)

name: Elena V. Shevchenko
title: Professor of Chemistry & Senior Scientist, Argonne National Laboratory
bio: Prof. Shevchenko studies self-assembly of colloidal nanoparticles into binary and ternary superlattices, creating artificial solid-state materials with engineered optical, electronic, and magnetic cooperative properties.
publications: Three-dimensional multi-component nanoparticle superlattices, Science (2023)
Dynamic phase transitions in co-crystallizing magnetic nanoparticles, JACS (2021)

name: Giulia Galli
degrees: Ph.D., International School for Advanced Studies (SISSA)
title: Liew Family Professor of Molecular Engineering and Chemistry
accolades: American Academy of Arts and Sciences
bio: Prof. Galli is an international leader in ab initio quantum simulations of matter, focusing on point defects in wide-bandgap semiconductors for quantum sensing and quantum computation, as well as electronic properties of renewable energy materials.
publications: Spin defects in semiconductors for quantum technologies: Predictions from first principles, PRX Quantum (2023)
Dielectric properties and electronic structure of liquid water under extreme pressures, PNAS (2022)

name: Greg Engel
title: Professor of Chemistry & Molecular Engineering; Director of Midwest Integrated Center for Quantum Materials
office: Gordon Center for Integrative Science W107
bio: Prof. Engel pioneered 2D electronic spectroscopy experiments that uncovered long-lived electronic quantum coherence in photosynthetic complexes, advancing understanding of quantum transport in biological light-harvesting.
publications: Quantum coherence in photosynthetic complexes under physiological conditions, Nature (2023)
Ultrafast excitonic energy transfer pathways in artificial multi-chromophore arrays, JACS (2022)

name: Guangbin Dong
title: Weldon G. Brown Professor of Chemistry
bio: Prof. Dong's group develops new catalytic paradigms for activating inert carbon-carbon and carbon-hydrogen bonds, creating catalytic transformations that streamline the synthesis of complex natural products and medicinal drugs.
publications: Catalytic activation and cleavage of unstrained carbon-carbon bonds, Nature Chem. (2023)
Palladium/norbornene cooperative catalysis for skeletal restructuring of ketones, Science (2021)

name: Hannah M. Lant
title: Assistant Professor of Chemistry
bio: The Lant Laboratory synthesizes hierarchical porous frameworks and metal-organic cages designed to stabilize catalytic intermediates for solar water splitting, carbon capture, and multi-electron redox transformations.
publications: Spatial orchestration of multi-electron photocatalysts inside metal-organic frameworks, Chem. Sci. (2024)
Operando X-ray spectroscopy of water oxidation centers in MOF thin films, JACS (2023)

name: Hening Lin
title: Professor of Chemistry
bio: Prof. Lin investigates sirtuins and novel post-translational protein acylations (malonylation, succinylation, glutarylation). His lab discovers regulatory mechanisms governing metabolism, innate immunity, and cancer survival.
publications: Sirtuin deacylation regulates mitochondrial metabolic rewiring in tumor immunity, Nature (2023)
Targeting metabolic enzymes with activity-based chemical probes, ACS Chem. Biol. (2022)

name: Jie Zhou
title: Assistant Professor of Chemistry
bio: Prof. Zhou's research utilizes ultrafast laser spectroscopy and terahertz near-field microscopy to capture nonequilibrium charge and spin dynamics in correlated electronic systems and topological insulators.
publications: Terahertz near-field optical microscopy of phase transitions in correlated oxides, Nature Physics (2023)
Coherent lattice polarons in layered 2D chalcogenides, Nano Lett. (2022)

name: John S. Anderson
title: Associate Professor of Chemistry
bio: The Anderson Laboratory designs reactive transition metal complexes and conductive metal-organic frameworks featuring non-innocent radical ligands capable of facilitating multi-electron bond-forming reactions.
publications: High electrical conductivity and metallic behavior in 2D sulfur-linked MOFs, Science (2023)
Dinitrogen activation and functionalization by low-valent iron-chalcogenide clusters, JACS (2021)

name: Joseph A. Piccirilli
title: Professor of Biochemistry and Molecular Biology & Chemistry
office: Gordon Center for Integrative Science W228
bio: Prof. Piccirilli is an authority on the chemical mechanism of RNA catalysis. His lab investigates catalytic ribozymes, the spliceosome core, and retrotransposons using biochemical, crystallographic, and cryo-EM methodologies.
publications: Structural basis for RNA cleavage by the group II intron ribozyme, Nature Struct. Mol. Biol. (2023)
Mechanism of branch-site selection in eukaryotic pre-mRNA splicing, Science (2021)

name: Ka Yee C. Lee
title: David Lee Shillinglaw Distinguished Service Professor; Executive Vice President for Strategic Initiatives
bio: Prof. Lee's research focuses on the behavior of complex thin films and biomembranes, elucidating how lung surfactants operate at the alveolar interface and the molecular mechanisms of membrane disruption by amyloid peptides.
publications: Thermodynamic and structural consequences of cholesterol on lung surfactant lipid films, Biophys. J. (2023)
Molecular mechanisms of lipid extraction by antimicrobial peptides, Langmuir (2021)

name: Michael D. Hopkins
title: Professor of Chemistry
bio: Prof. Hopkins explores the electronic structure, bonding, and photophysics of conjugated metal-organic compounds. His laboratory designs tungsten and molybdenum alkylidyne complexes for nonlinear optical applications.
publications: Electronic delocalization in pi-conjugated metal-alkylidyne oligomers, Inorg. Chem. (2023)
Optical nonlinearities in transition metal coordination polymers, Chem. Mater. (2021)

name: Norbert F. Scherer
title: Professor of Chemistry & The James Franck Institute
bio: Prof. Scherer studies optical matter and nanoparticle assembly governed by light forces. His group creates dynamic optical lattices using electrodynamic interactions to direct matter at the nanoscale.
publications: Observation of non-reciprocal optical forces in structured light fields, Nature Photonics (2023)
Dynamic assembly and collective oscillations of optical matter arrays, Optica (2021)

name: Philippe Guyot-Sionnest
title: Professor of Chemistry and Physics
bio: Prof. Guyot-Sionnest is a pioneer in colloidal quantum dots and infrared optoelectronics. His group created the first colloidal quantum dot infrared lasers and detectors operating across mid- and far-infrared wavelengths.
publications: Intraband infrared photoluminescence and lasing in colloidal quantum dots, Nature Photonics (2023)
Hot electron relaxation dynamics in n-doped semiconductor nanocrystals, Nano Lett. (2021)

name: Raymond E. Moellering
title: Associate Professor of Chemistry
bio: Prof. Moellering's group develops chemoproteomic technologies to map reactive metabolite-protein modifications, discovering allosteric regulation sites and therapeutic vulnerabilities in aggressive human cancers.
publications: Chemoproteomic profiling reveals functional metabolic stress sensors in breast cancer, Cell Chem. Biol. (2023)
Targeting oncoprotein dimers with stapled peptide probes, PNAS (2021)

name: Sarah B. King
title: Assistant Professor of Chemistry
bio: Prof. King investigates electronic dynamics at nanoscale interfaces using time-resolved photoemission electron microscopy (TR-PEEM), tracking charge separation and exciton diffusion in next-generation photovoltaics.
publications: Direct visualization of spatial exciton diffusion in MoS2/WS2 heterobilayers, Nat. Commun. (2023)
Ultrafast charge injection dynamics at organic-semiconductor junctions, J. Phys. Chem. C (2022)

name: Scott A. Snyder
title: Professor of Chemistry
bio: Prof. Snyder designs concise, general synthetic strategies to construct complex bioactive natural products, inventing novel reagents for selective halogenation and polycyclic architectures.
publications: Total synthesis of complex halogenated marine alkaloids via biomimetic cascades, Nature Chem. (2023)
Programmable reagent platforms for stereoselective halofunctionalization, JACS (2021)

name: Shaunna M. McLeod
title: Assistant Professor of Chemistry
bio: Prof. McLeod's laboratory investigates bacterial enzymatic pathways involved in antibiotic resistance and cell wall biosynthesis, developing chemical inhibitors that restore antibiotic susceptibility.
publications: Structural characterization of peptidoglycan transglycosylase inhibition, Biochemistry (2023)
Mechanism of allosteric regulation in bacterial cell envelope enzymes, J. Biol. Chem. (2021)

name: Steven J. Sibener
title: Carl William Eisendrath Distinguished Service Professor of Chemistry & The James Franck Institute
bio: Prof. Sibener is a pioneer in surface and materials chemistry. His laboratory utilizes supersonic molecular beam scattering and variable-temperature scanning probe microscopy to study gas-surface reaction dynamics.
publications: Direct visualization of atomic-scale corrosion and passivation on metal single crystals, Science (2023)
Supersonic beam scattering investigations of energy transfer at gas-polymer interfaces, PNAS (2021)

name: Stuart J. Rowan
title: Barry L. MacLean Professor of Molecular Engineering and Chemistry
bio: Prof. Rowan develops stimuli-responsive supramolecular polymers, dynamic covalent networks (vitrimers), and bio-derived nanocomposites capable of autonomous healing, shape-memory transitions, and chemical recycling.
publications: Circularly recyclable thermosets based on dynamic boronic ester networks, Nature Materials (2023)
Mechanically adaptive nanocomposites inspired by sea cucumber dermis, Science (2021)

name: Suri Vaikuntanathan
title: Professor of Chemistry & The James Franck Institute
bio: Prof. Vaikuntanathan's group studies the statistical mechanics of driven systems, active matter, and self-assembly out of equilibrium, formulating principles of efficiency, dissipative work, and information harvesting.
publications: Thermodynamic uncertainty relations in active multi-particle fluids, Phys. Rev. X (2023)
Controlling self-assembly pathways using non-equilibrium dissipation, Nature Physics (2022)

name: Viresh H. Rawal
title: Professor of Chemistry
bio: Prof. Rawal developed the widely used squaramide and TADDOL-based chiral hydrogen-bonding organocatalysts, pioneering stereoselective cycloadditions and asymmetric methods for pharmaceutical synthesis.
publications: Enantioselective organocatalysis via dual hydrogen-bond donors, Chem. Rev. (2023)
Total synthesis of complex indole alkaloids via catalytic asymmetric cycloadditions, JACS (2021)

name: Weixin Tang
degrees: Ph.D., University of Illinois at Urbana-Champaign
title: Assistant Professor of Chemistry
bio: Prof. Tang creates precision molecular recording and genome-editing technologies. Her laboratory develops continuous directed evolution platforms to engineer next-generation base editors and prime editors.
publications: Continuous directed evolution of precision base editors in mammalian cells, Nature Biotech. (2023)
Engineered DNA polymerases for cellular event recording, Nature Chemical Biology (2021)

name: Wenbin Lin
degrees: Ph.D., University of Illinois at Urbana-Champaign
title: James Franck Professor of Chemistry
bio: Prof. Lin pioneered nanoscale metal-organic frameworks (nMOFs) and nanoscale coordination polymers (NCPs) for clinical cancer immunotherapy, radio-sensitization, and solar fuel photocatalysis.
publications: Nanoscale metal-organic frameworks for enhanced checkpoint blockade immunotherapy, Nature Biomed. Eng. (2023)
Single-site catalysts in metal-organic frameworks for artificial photosynthesis, Chem. Rev. (2022)
